Control requirement: Provide a list of connections in the "List of Connections" tab, including interactive and non-interactive access, connections to other public cloud services, and connections to external systems.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: inventory management-plane and applicable data-plane connections. Logical scopes have administrative/API relationships, not independent network listeners.

Control requirement: Baseline configuration standards should be established for the cloud service.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: Bank-approved baseline, Azure Policy where supported, and manual checks. This is not proof of full CIS coverage for every resource type.

Control requirement: Describe the control in place for segregation of production and test environments.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: environment isolation by subscription, identity, resource and network design. Shared tenant/platform services require scoped separation rather than duplicate instances.

Control requirement: Where service mode is IaaS or PaaS, Bank-approved anti-virus / anti-malware and host-based intrusion prevention system should be implemented.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y only for customer-managed VM guest OS. NA elsewhere means host-agent installation is Microsoft-managed or outside this resource function; application security remains applicable. Functions customer code still requires security controls.

Control requirement: Cloud service provider should ensure penetration testing has been performed covering OWASP Top vulnerabilities, CWE Top 25, and applicable API/microservice threats.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: provider assurance and applicable workload penetration-testing evidence must be obtained. Y does NOT confirm a test occurred or that SOC/OSPAR proves OWASP/CWE coverage.

Control requirement: Does the cloud service support and enable integration with the Bank's Azure Active Directory (AD) for all interactive user authentication?
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: Entra-authenticated management access; validate service data-plane/local authentication separately. Managed Identity is non-interactive (NA).

Control requirement: State the specific protocol supported for Azure AD integration (e.g. SAML 2.0).
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: document actual Entra authentication/token protocols; OAuth 2.0 is authorization, OIDC authentication. Do not assume SAML for every Azure service.

Control requirement: Describe the supported interactive user authentication mechanisms that will be enabled.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: Entra interactive sign-in, approved MFA and emergency access design. Emergency cloud-only accounts still depend on Entra availability.

Control requirement: Authentication mechanism should enforce minimum 12-character passwords with alphabetic and numeric/special characters.
Assessment basis / caveat: N for inherited Entra cloud-only baseline: tenant-wide 12-character minimum cannot be configured natively. Bank AD enforcement or documented credential provisioning may change the assessment. VM guest password policies must also be assessed.

Control requirement: Password controls: non-null, no reuse of last 5 passwords, maximum validity period, mandatory expiry changes.
Assessment basis / caveat: N for inherited cloud-only baseline: configurable last-five-password history is not available. Bank authoritative identity policies and exceptions require review; do not infer compliance.

Control requirement: Force password change upon first login using temporary/issued password.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: account onboarding supports temporary-password first-login change, subject to authoritative identity system; managed centrally for most resources.

Control requirement: Passwords should be issued securely; avoid clear-text email delivery.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: Bank process for secure credential issuance, inherited for services using central identity. Not a claim the Azure resource issues passwords.

Control requirement: Support password change by authenticated users at any time.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: password change through authoritative Entra/AD process; review hybrid writeback and guest OS separately.

Control requirement: Store passwords in irreversible cryptographic format using approved algorithms.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: inherited identity password-verifier protection. No claim that each resource stores end-user passwords; validate provider/OS cryptographic evidence.

Control requirement: Protect stored passwords using strong access controls and least privilege.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: inherited identity protections and least-privilege administration. Review VM local credentials separately.

Control requirement: Passwords must not be returned to clients in any form for verification.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: authentication should not return the stored user password. Secret retrieval APIs and VM deployment credentials are separate use cases requiring protection.

Control requirement: Protect printed passwords from disclosure and tampering.
Assessment basis / caveat: NA assumes electronic-only credential handling and no printed passwords. Change to Y and assess physical safeguards if printed emergency credentials exist.

Control requirement: Automatically disable/lock accounts after configurable failed login attempts.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: inherited Entra smart lockout; custom settings/licensing and hybrid/VM local lockout require validation.

Control requirement: Logon failure messages must not reveal whether username or password is incorrect.
Assessment basis / caveat: N is conservative: generic error wording cannot be guaranteed across Microsoft-managed sign-in flows. Assess actual flows and obtain exception/compensating controls where needed.

Control requirement: Default passwords should be changed before go-live.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for VM deployment/local passwords and Entra initial/emergency credential provisioning. NA for resources with no customer default-password account; service keys assessed under 2.5/2.7.

Control requirement: MFA should be enabled for Internet-facing services and privileged/administrative access.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: inherited MFA for human management access; application end-user and VM guest access need separate validation. NA for Managed Identity because it is non-interactive, not exempt from workload identity security.

Control requirement: Describe non-interactive authentication mechanisms (API keys, tokens, secrets, etc.).
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: document management/API automation identity and applicable service credentials. Entra administration of logical scopes is also non-interactive API access.

Control requirement: Credentials used by systems/applications should support regular rotation.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: managed identity credential lifecycle or customer credential/certificate/key rotation, including credentials used by automation managing the resource. Does not imply every resource has its own secret.

Control requirement: State where credentials are stored and how they are protected.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: approved secret store for customer credentials and protected identity-platform storage for provider-managed credentials. Managed identity underlying credentials are not placed in customer Key Vault.

Control requirement: Confirm all hard-coded or default credentials are changed before go-live.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: deployment/source/configuration checks for hard-coded and default credentials, including automation managing logical resources; requires evidence, not a completed-state assertion.

Control requirement: Unused default accounts should be deleted or disabled.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for Entra identity inventory and VM local accounts. NA elsewhere means no independent default user account in assessed resource scope; application accounts require separate review.

Control requirement: Support central management of security policies across multiple cloud services.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: central governance through appropriate Azure Policy, Entra roles, RBAC and manual controls; not all controls/resources have native policy coverage.

Control requirement: Support segregation of duties through granular administrative role assignment.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: scope-specific roles, least privilege and segregation of duties; assess directory roles and data-plane roles separately.

Control requirement: Support maker-checker controls for user and role administration functions.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y via Bank IAM approval workflow and restricted direct administration. PIM activation approval does not approve every account/role change.

Control requirement: Support maker-checker controls for sensitive functions.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y via Bank change approvals, protected IaC pipelines and restricted bypass. Resource locks alone do not implement maker-checker.

Control requirement: Automatically terminate idle sessions after configurable inactivity period.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for inherited Azure Portal directory idle timeout; VM/Bastion/CLI/application sessions require separate controls. Sign-in frequency is not idle termination. NA for non-interactive Managed Identity.

Control requirement: Prevent concurrent logons using the same account from different workstations.
Assessment basis / caveat: N: no general Entra/Azure management single-session enforcement across workstations. A verified app/PAM control may change the finding. Named accounts/MFA do not satisfy this alone.

Control requirement: Automatically revoke or disable inactive accounts after 30 days.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y only through configured Bank AD/Entra lifecycle automation for human identities; not a default 30-day native guarantee. Managed Identity human-account inactivity is NA; review workload identity lifecycle separately.

Control requirement: Enforce least privilege and deny-by-default access controls.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: least-privilege identity/service authorization and explicit network controls where relevant. Default NSG rules do not establish deny-all east-west isolation.

Control requirement: Enable network access controls (e.g. IP whitelisting) where Internet access is not required.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: appropriate private endpoints, service firewall/network controls for data plane, and Conditional Access for supported human management access. Do not treat CA as a service firewall or assume every resource has a private endpoint.

Control requirement: Group containers with similar risk profiles together.
Assessment basis / caveat: NA assumes no container workloads in scope; a VM/Functions container deployment requires reassessment.

Control requirement: Adopt container-specific security solutions.
Assessment basis / caveat: NA assumes no container workloads in scope; image scanning/runtime controls become applicable if containers are introduced.

Control requirement: Implement stringent controls for container orchestrator access.
Assessment basis / caveat: NA: no container orchestrator included in the supplied service list. Reassess if AKS or another orchestrator is present.

Control requirement: Support robust authentication and service mesh for API access control.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for application/API execution on VM/Functions, requiring authn/authz plus mesh assessment. NA elsewhere is the service-mesh/application implementation scope, not exemption of service management APIs from authentication. No mesh is assumed deployed.

Control requirement: Use internationally recognized cryptographic standards.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: approved cryptography for applicable management transport, stored configuration and data. Confirm algorithms by service; not all resources encrypt customer payloads.

Control requirement: Encrypt sensitive credentials in transit and at rest.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: protect any credential in management/integration transport or storage; use approved secret stores. Logical network resources do not independently store application credentials.

Control requirement: Encrypt confidential or sensitive data in transit and at rest.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for data/configuration protection at the appropriate platform, application or transport layer. ExpressRoute private peering is not inherently encryption; additional encryption is needed where required.

Control requirement: Cryptographic keys should not be hardcoded.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: prevent embedded customer keys in code, IaC, scripts and configuration. Applies also to automation administering logical resources.

Control requirement: Support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK).
Assessment basis / caveat: Y only for Key Vault key import and Storage/VM disk customer-managed encryption use cases in this initial scope. N for other payload/log services pending SKU/feature-specific BYOK verification, NOT a definitive unsupported finding. NA for resource functions without customer encryption-key import/selection. Functions backing Storage is assessed under Storage.

Control requirement: Store cryptographic keys in FIPS140-2 Level 3 certified HSM.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y only for Key Vault with actual HSM-protected key type and acceptable validation; confirm Premium or add Managed HSM as a separate service. N for customer data/log services until key architecture, SKU and FIPS acceptance are verified. NA for non-key-custody/control-plane functions. FIPS 140-3 acceptance against 140-2 requirement needs Bank approval.

Control requirement: Support Bring Your Own Encryption (BYOE).
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for VM/Functions application encryption and Storage/messaging opaque encrypted payloads using an approved upstream encryptor. NA for platform/control-plane functions without independent BYOE workload scope. Customer-managed platform keys alone are not BYOE.

Control requirement: Support secure key rotation.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: centralized customer key lifecycle in Key Vault, including update of dependent services; for VM/application keys assess customer implementation. NA elsewhere means lifecycle assessed under Key Vault/owner, not permission to retain stale keys.

Control requirement: Support secure key destruction.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for Key Vault deletion/purge lifecycle and customer-controlled VM application keys, subject to retention. NA other resource functions: key destruction assessed in owning key-management system. Y does not mean instant purge.

Control requirement: Use cryptographic keys for single purposes only.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for customer key inventory/use in Key Vault and VM/Functions application code. NA elsewhere means key-purpose enforcement belongs to upstream key owner; platform consumers still require design review.

Control requirement: Allow immediate key revocation, destruction, and replacement upon compromise.
Assessment basis / caveat: N for Key Vault/customer-key consumers: full immediate revocation + destruction + replacement is not assured because of purge retention, caches and dependent-service behavior. NA other resources have no independent customer-key destruction function. Validate incident procedure and any alternative architecture.

Control requirement: Describe controls protecting data in multi-tenant environments.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: provider isolation assurance plus Bank identity, network and data controls. Logical scopes rely on platform isolation, not dedicated host tenancy.

Control requirement: Scan uploaded files for malware before processing or storage.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for Storage/VM/Functions file-handling workflows, only with upstream scanning or quarantine/release gates. Defender for Storage scans after upload, not before storage. NA others assumes no file-upload workflow; reassess ACS attachments, message payloads and other ingestion if present.

Control requirement: Ensure passwords, credentials, and keys are not logged in audit trails.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: prevent secrets in native/custom logs, scripts and diagnostics; do not assume the platform can redact every customer-generated field.

Control requirement: Maintain audit logs for all access and administrative activities.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: management audit logging plus service data-plane/application/OS logs where relevant; not a claim every operation is covered natively.

Control requirement: Record successful and failed security-relevant events.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: identity, control-plane and workload security events as applicable; document event gaps and supplemental logging.

Control requirement: Audit records should contain required event details.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: platform fields supplemented by application/OS records where required; verify sample records against Bank schema.

Control requirement: Audit all administration activities with detailed records.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y: management and identity audit records with IaC/change/OS evidence for missing before-after values or commands; full details not guaranteed by Activity Log alone.

Control requirement: Protect audit trails from unauthorized modification.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y via restricted central logging and immutable storage where required; not a claim each source service provides immutable audit storage.

Control requirement: Support transfer of audit logs to the Bank's SIEM.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y via supported central collection/export paths, Entra/service connectors, Event Hubs or approved integrations. Not every resource has independent diagnostic settings. Alert-only export needs explicit approval if raw logs are required.

Control requirement: Support monitoring and alerting for suspicious activities.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y via central SOC detections using relevant identity, activity, service and workload signals; no claim every service has a dedicated Defender plan.

Control requirement: Implement multi-tier architecture for Internet-facing solutions.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for resources that can implement, route, secure or host Internet-facing tiers. NA for other resource roles; a Y for a routing component does not mean it is Internet-exposed. Validate whole-solution architecture.

Control requirement: Implement multi-tier architecture for private leased-line connectivity.
Assessment basis / caveat: Y for resources that can implement, route, secure or host privately connected tiers. ExpressRoute/Virtual WAN routes must explicitly traverse required inspection points; private links are not inherently encrypted. NA for other resource roles.
